name: Worktrunk
one_liner: Manages Git worktrees for running several coding agents in parallel.

text.why: Attach several agents at once and branches and working folders begin to overwrite each other. worktrunk reduces creating, switching and removing Git worktrees to single commands, assuming a flow where every agent gets its own isolated folder. It is a CLI written in Rust; no license is declared in the repository, so check that before adopting it.
text.take: Addressing worktrees by branch name removes the actual friction in running agents in parallel.
build: An internal flow that gives every agent its own working folder
An end-of-day script that clears finished parallel work

who.situation: gives each agent its own working folder
opens a PR branch straight into a worktree

start.text: brew install worktrunk && wt config shell install

caveat: GitHub metadata shows no license; the README badge says MIT OR Apache-2.0
Shell integration (wt config shell install) is required to change directories
On Windows wt clashes with Windows Terminal, so it installs as git-wt

numbers.star_delta_unit: GitHub stars gained in the window, GH Archive events summed to as_of
numbers.method: Star total = the value last checked on GitHub (stars_checked_at) + increases observed via GH Archive since. The 24h · 7d · 30d gains are GH Archive hourly events summed to the reference time (as_of). No score of ours.
